newsitem.title: USA: U.S. orders 160 Americans to leave Albania.
newsitem.headline: U.S. orders 160 Americans to leave Albania.

text.p: The United States on Wednesday ordered 160 U.S. government employees and their dependants to leave Albania because of worsening instability there.
The State Department said it had also urged the estimated 2,000 private Americans living in Albania to leave the country.

Spokesman Nicholas Burns said U.S. fears about the Albanian crisis had grown because insurgents had not accepted a peace proposal put forward by President Sali Berisha and large numbers of armed civilians had broken into depots and stolen weapons, creating a highly volatile situation.

"In the view of the concerns we have about the security situation in Albania, we are ordering a drawdown of non-essential United States government personnel in Albania ...Dependents and non-essential personnel will depart Albania in the coming days," he said.
In addition, he said, "we are advising American citizens to consider departing Albania as soon as possible."

Burns said there were roughly 2,000 private Americans in Albania. The 160 U.S. government employees and their dependents include 74 Peace Corps volunteers, 39 State Department employees and dependents, 54 U.S. Agency for International Development contractors and their dependents. The rest are U.S. Information Agency-sponsored individuals and Fulbright scholars. U.S. Ambassador Marisa Lino and 17 other diplomats will remain, Burns said.
